quotes: A non-sensitive, 8-yr-old male patient (termed UV81KO) with only acute recurrent sunburns and without any other physical or neuromental retardations was studied.
The patient's skin exhibited lowered minimal erythema doses between 280 and 300 nm monochromatic wavelengths without delayed peaking of erythema.
The base line level of sister-chromatid exchanges (SCEs) was higher in UV81KO cells (10-12 SCEs/cell) than in normal cells (5 SCEs/cell)

records.segregation: inheritance of two heterozygous missense mutations from heterozygous parents confirmed
quotes: In this study we assess the cellular markers in two independent families that included two photosensitive patients that were identified as xeroderma pigmentosum variant.
In one family, we confirmed inheritance of two heterozygous mis-sense mutations. One mutation is an A-->G transition at nucleotide 1840 that generates a K535E mis-sense mutation.
Another mutation is an A-->C transversion at nucleotide 2003 that generates a K589 mis-sense mutation.

notes.statement: Using DNA combing, Despras et al. (2010) showed that the translesion synthesis defect in XP-V cells led to a strong reduction in active replication forks and a high proportion of stalled forks after UV irradiation, with extensive single-strand DNA formation and over-activation of the ATR/Chk1 pathway after low UVC doses.
quotes: Using DNA combing, we showed that translesion synthesis defect leads to a strong reduction in the number of active replication forks and a high proportion of stalled forks in human cells, which contrasts with budding yeast.
extensive regions of single-strand DNA are formed during replication in irradiated XP-V cells, leading to an over-activation of ATR/Chk1 pathway after low UVC doses.

notes.statement: Despras et al. (2010) found that low-dose caffeine after irradiation decreased Chk1 activation and abrogated DNA synthesis in XP-V cells, and that Chk1 inhibition by UCN-01 increased fork stalling and sensitized XP-V cells to UVC as caffeine does. They concluded that in the absence of pol-eta, Chk1 becomes essential for replication resumption via fork stabilization, providing an explanation for the caffeine sensitivity of XP-V cells.
quotes: Addition of a low concentration of caffeine post-irradiation, although inefficient to restore S-phase progression, significantly decreases Chk1 activation and abrogates DNA synthesis in XP-V cells.
Consequently, UCN-01 sensitizes XP-V cells to UVC as caffeine does.
In the absence of poleta, Chk1 kinase becomes essential for replication resumption by alternative pathways, via fork stabilization.

notes.statement: Cleaver et al. (1980) concluded that a pigmented xerodermoid cell culture was indistinguishable from the XP variant in UV-induced unscheduled DNA synthesis, strand breakage during repair, chain growth during semiconservative replication with or without caffeine, and recovery of replication, so the term 'pigmented xerodermoid' was redundant.
quotes: It is concluded that a pigmented xerodermoid cell culture is indistinguishable from the XP variant and the former term is therefore redundant.
The "pigmented xerodermoid" was previously defined on the basis of mild clinical symptoms that suggested it might be similar to but distinct from xeroderma pigmentosum (XP).

notes.statement: Cleaver et al. (1980) proposed that the defect in XP variant cells was the loss of a gene product that lets normal cells replicate DNA without interruption at UV-induced pyrimidine dimers. As a result, replication forks were blocked more often and at lower doses. They suggested that the link between this defect and the high rate of actinic carcinogenesis pointed to an important role for disturbed DNA replication in human carcinogenesis.
quotes: The defect common to these cell types appears to be the loss of a gene product that permits normal cells to replicate DNA without interruption at damaged sites (u.v.-induced pyrimidine dimers).
The consequence of this loss is that replication forks are blocked more frequently and at lower doses in XP variant cells.
The correlation between this defect and high levels of actinic carcinogenesis in these patients points to an important role for perturbations in DNA replication in human carcinogenesis.

notes.statement: Itoh et al. (2000) noted that among hereditary photosensitive disorders, only XPV cells showed normal unscheduled DNA synthesis and normal recovery of RNA synthesis but reduced recovery of replicative DNA synthesis after UV (51% of normal), which was further reduced to 36% in the presence of nontoxic caffeine.
quotes: only xeroderma pigmentosum variant cells exhibited normal unscheduled DNA synthesis, normal recovery of RNA synthesis, but reduced recovery of replicative DNA synthesis (51 +/- 6% the rate relative to normal controls).
This reduction of recovery of replicative DNA synthesis was enhanced in the presence of a nontoxic level of caffeine to 36 +/- 5%.

notes.statement: Itoh et al. (2000) found that cells from heterozygous parents of XPV patients had normal UDS, RNA synthesis recovery, and replicative DNA synthesis recovery, but reduced recovery of replicative DNA synthesis in the presence of 1 mM caffeine (53% of normal) and slightly reduced UV survival with caffeine. They suggested that XPV heterozygotes can be identified by UV sensitivity in the presence of nontoxic caffeine.
quotes: Cells from heterozygotic parents showed normal levels of unscheduled DNA synthesis, recovery of RNA synthesis, and recovery of replicative DNA synthesis, but reduced rates of recovery of replicative DNA synthesis in the presence of 1 mM caffeine (53 +/- 8% relative to the normal control).
the cells showed normal survival by ultraviolet without caffeine, but slightly reduced survival by ultraviolet with 1 mM caffeine present.
These results suggest that xeroderma pigmentosum variant heterozygotes can be identified by their sensitivity to ultraviolet irradiation in the presence of nontoxic levels of caffeine.

notes.statement: Itoh et al. (2000) found that neither the K535E nor the K589 missense mutation identified in an XPV family was present in 52 unrelated Japanese individuals.
quotes: Each of these mutations were absent in 52 unrelated Japanese individuals.

notes.statement: Johnson et al. (1999) identified nonsense or frameshift mutations in hRAD30, the human counterpart of yeast RAD30, in XP variant cell lines. Of the 8 mutations identified, 7 were predicted to result in a severely truncated hRad30 protein, indicating that defects in hRAD30 cause XP-V.
quotes: Here it is shown that XP variant (XP-V) cell lines harbor nonsense or frameshift mutations in hRAD30, the human counterpart of yeast RAD30.
Of the eight mutations identified, seven would result in a severely truncated hRad30 protein. These results indicate that defects in hRAD30 cause XP-V

notes.statement: Johnson et al. (1999) noted that yeast RAD30 encodes a DNA polymerase involved in error-free bypass of UV damage, and suggested that error-free replication of UV lesions by hRad30 plays an important role in minimizing the incidence of sunlight-induced skin cancers.
quotes: Yeast RAD30 encodes a DNA polymerase involved in the error-free bypass of ultraviolet (UV) damage.
they suggest that error-free replication of UV lesions by hRad30 plays an important role in minimizing the incidence of sunlight-induced skin cancers.

notes.statement: Masutani et al. (1999) noted that xeroderma pigmentosum variant is an inherited disorder with an increased incidence of sunlight-induced skin cancers. Unlike cells from XP groups A to G, XP-V cells carry out normal nucleotide-excision repair but are defective in replicating UV-damaged DNA.
quotes: Xeroderma pigmentosum variant (XP-V) is an inherited disorder which is associated with increased incidence of sunlight-induced skin cancers.
XP-V cells carry out normal nucleotide-excision repair processes but are defective in their replication of ultraviolet-damaged DNA.

notes.statement: Using a cell-free trans-lesion synthesis assay, Masutani et al. (1999) isolated a DNA polymerase from HeLa cells that bypassed UV-induced thymine dimers in XP-V cell extracts. They identified it as a human homolog of yeast Rad30 (DNA polymerase eta), a member of the UmuC/DinB/Rev1 family of damage-bypass replication proteins.
quotes: we have recently isolated a DNA polymerase from HeLa cells that continues replication on damaged DNA by bypassing ultraviolet-induced thymine dimers in XP-V cell extracts
Here we show that this polymerase is a human homologue of the yeast Rad30 protein, recently identified as DNA polymerase eta.

notes.statement: Masutani et al. (1999) found mutations in the DNA polymerase eta gene in all XP-V cells they examined. Recombinant human DNA polymerase eta corrected the inability of XP-V cell extracts to replicate DNA past thymine dimers. The authors concluded that DNA polymerase eta could be the XPV gene product.
quotes: We found that all XP-V cells examined carry mutations in their DNA polymerase eta gene.
Recombinant human DNA polymerase eta corrects the inability of XP-V cell extracts to carry out DNA replication by bypassing thymine dimers on damaged DNA.

notes.statement: Itoh et al. (1996) described a simple autoradiographic method for diagnosing XP variant. It measures three DNA repair markers in patient fibroblasts and compares them with adjacent normal cells on the same coverslips: unscheduled DNA synthesis, recovery of RNA synthesis, and recovery of replicative DNA synthesis after UV irradiation. Among hereditary photosensitive disorders (XP, Cockayne syndrome, UV-sensitive syndrome), only XPV cells showed normal UDS and normal RNA synthesis recovery but reduced recovery of replicative DNA synthesis, at about 50% of control.
quotes: We present here an alternative simple method for the diagnosis of xeroderma pigmentosum variant that measures three cellular markers for DNA repair by autoradiography, unscheduled DNA synthesis, recovery of RNA synthesis, and recovery of replicative DNA synthesis after ultraviolet irradiation.

only xeroderma pigmentosum variant cells exhibit normal unscheduled DNA synthesis, normal recovery of RNA synthesis, but reduced recovery of replicative DNA synthesis (approximately 50% of that of control cells).

notes.statement: Itoh et al. (1996) found that caffeine enhanced the reduced recovery of replicative DNA synthesis after UV irradiation in XPV cells. Because each photosensitive disorder gave a different combination of the three markers, the authors proposed that the method also provides a systematic basis for diagnosing these diseases.
quotes: This reduction of DNA synthesis is enhanced in the presence of caffeine.
Because each disorder yields a different combination of these three markers, this method also provides a systematic basis for the diagnosis of these diseases.

notes.statement: Fujiwara et al. (1981) found that fibroblasts from the photosensitive patient UV81KO were 5-fold more sensitive than normal cells to killing by 254-nm UV. However, the cells showed no detectable defect in nucleotide excision repair or in replicative bypass. They did fail to recover DNA synthesis after UV irradiation at doses at which normal cells recovered.
quotes: UV81KO skin fibroblasts in culture was 5-fold more sensitive to 254 nm UV killing than normal cells, though the response of obligatory heterozygotes was normal.
indicated no apparently detectable defects in nucleotide-excision repair processes and in replicative bypass in UV81KO cells.
UV81KO cells showed the defective recovery of DNA synthesis after 254 nm UV irradiation with 1 and 5 J/m2, at which dose the recovery occurred in normal cells.

notes.statement: Fujiwara et al. (1981) concluded that the clinical, cellular and molecular features of UV81KO set it clearly apart from xeroderma pigmentosum, Cockayne syndrome, the 11961 disorder and Bloom syndrome. They proposed it as a new photodermatosis with a defect in the recovery of DNA synthesis after UV exposure.
quotes: Such clinical, cellular and molecular characteristics and comparison to those in the other photodermatoses (xeroderma pigmentosum, Cockayne's syndrome, the 11961 disorder, Bloom's syndrome) can make a clear distinction of UV81KO from the others.
the UV81KO disorder is put forward as a new photodermatosis with a defect in the recovery of post-UV DNA synthesis.

notes.statement: Cleaver (1972) described variants of xeroderma pigmentosum that had normal DNA repair and normal sensitivity to ultraviolet light.
quotes: Xeroderma pigmentosum: variants with normal DNA repair and normal sensitivity to ultraviolet light.

notes.statement: Robbins et al. (1974) reviewed xeroderma pigmentosum as an inherited disease with sun sensitivity, multiple cutaneous neoplasms, and abnormal DNA repair.
quotes: Xeroderma pigmentosum. An inherited diseases with sun sensitivity, multiple cutaneous neoplasms, and abnormal DNA repair.

notes.statement: Wang et al. (1991) transfected an XP variant cell line with a UV-irradiated shuttle vector carrying the supF gene as a mutation target. Mutant frequency increased linearly with dose, with a slope 5 times steeper than in normal cells. Of 53 independent mutants, 52 had base substitutions, and 62 of the 64 substitutions involved a dipyrimidine.
quotes: The frequency of mutants increased linearly with dose, but with a slope 5 times steeper than that seen with normal cells.

Sequence analysis of the supF gene showed that 52 of 53 independent mutants generated in the XP variant cells contained base substitutions, with 62 of 64 of the substitutions involving a dipyrimidine.

notes.statement: Wang et al. (1991) found that 28% of the mutations in XP variant cells involved A.T base pairs, compared with 11% in normal cells. Most were at position 136, the middle of a run of three A.T base pairs. If the excision rate is the same in both cell lines, the authors suggested that XP variant cells are less likely than normal cells to incorporate dAMP opposite photoproduct bases. They proposed that this could account for the UV hypermutability of XP variant cells.
quotes: Twenty-eight percent of the mutations involved A.T base pairs, with the majority found at position 136, the middle of a run of three A.T base pairs. (In the normal cells, this value was only 11%.)

our data suggest that XP variant cells are less likely than normal cells to incorporate dAMP opposite bases involved in photo-products. If such incorporation also occurs during replication of chromosomal DNA, this could account for the hypermutability of XP variant cells with UV irradiation.

notes.statement: Wang et al. (1991) noted that XP variant patients show the clinical features of xeroderma pigmentosum, including more skin cancer. However, their cells have a normal or nearly normal rate of nucleotide excision repair and are only slightly more sensitive than normal cells to UV cytotoxicity. The cells are significantly more sensitive to the mutagenic effect of UV.
quotes: Xeroderma pigmentosum (XP) variant patients show the clinical characteristics of the disease, with increased frequencies of skin cancer, but their cells have a normal, or nearly normal, rate of nucleotide excision repair of UV-induced DNA damage and are only slightly more sensitive than normal cells to the cytotoxic effect of UV radiation.
However, they are significantly more sensitive to its mutagenic effect.

notes.statement: Lehmann et al. (1975) noted that cells from most patients with xeroderma pigmentosum cannot excise UV-induced pyrimidine dimers. One class of patients, however, has cells that are completely normal in this excision repair process.
quotes: Cells cultured from most patients suffering from the sunlight-sensitive hereditary disorder xeroderma pigmentosum are defective in the ability to excise ultraviolet light (UV)-induced pyrimidine dimers from their DNA. There is, however, one class of these patients whose cells are completely normal in this excision repair process.

notes.statement: Lehmann et al. (1975) found that XP variant cells, which have normal excision repair, synthesize DNA abnormally after UV irradiation. Newly synthesized low-molecular-weight DNA took much longer than in normal cells to be converted to high-molecular-weight DNA. This slow conversion was drastically inhibited by caffeine, which had no effect in normal cells.
quotes: We have found that these cells have an abnormality in the manner in which DNA is synthesized after UV-irradiation.

The time taken to convert initially low-molecular-weight DNA synthesized in UV-irradiated cells into high-molecular-weight DNA similar in size to that in untreated cells is much greater in these variants than in normal cells.
Furthermore, this slow conversion of low to high-molecular-weight newly synthesized DNA is drastically inhibited by caffeine, which has no effect in normal cells.

notes.statement: Lehmann et al. (1975) found that two cell lines from excision-defective classes of xeroderma pigmentosum showed intermediate effects. Both the time needed to convert newly synthesized DNA to high molecular weight and the caffeine inhibition of this process were in between normal and XP variant cells.
quotes: Two cell lines from classes of xeroderma pigmentosum that are defective in excision-repair show intermediate effects, with regard to both the time taken to convert newly synthesized DNA to high molecular weight and the inhibition of this process by caffeine.
